Tom Cruise, Anne Hathaway confirm release date for 'Days of Thunder 2'

By Samuel Stubbs  |  Last updated Aug 29, 2026 2:04 PM ET
Add us as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 13:09
Instaread

It's been known that a sequel to the 1990 NASCAR-centric film "Days of Thunder" was in the works, but Tom Cruise and Anne Hathaway confirmed a general release date for the film in a social media post on Saturday. 

In a video filmed at Daytona International Speedway, the site of Saturday's Cup Series race (7:30 p.m. ET, NBC) Hathaway and Cruise posed in front of a Next-Gen car bearing a green and yellow Days of Thunder-themed paint scheme. 

"We're coming out summer of 2028," Cruise said. "Don't be late."

What a Days of Thunder sequel will mean to NASCAR

Released as NASCAR began to boom at the start of the 1990s, "Days of Thunder" centers around Cruise, who plays a young driver -- Cole Trickle, who is new to the stock car racing scene. Along with crew chief Harry Hogge, played by the late Robert Duvall, Trickle navigates rivalries with Rowdy Burns and Russ Wheeler, recovers from an injury suffered in a harrowing crash at Daytona and eventually returns to Daytona to win the Daytona 500. 

Days of Thunder. Summer 2028. pic.twitter.com/rD3QLXfUyi

— Tom Cruise (@TomCruise) August 29, 2026

It's unknown whether Cruise, who will be 66 in the summer of 2028, will still play a character who is actively racing. The oldest winner in NASCAR Cup Series history is Harry Gant, who won at Michigan in Aug. 1992 at age 52.

A sequel to the beloved film is a massive opportunity for NASCAR to get back into the American mainstream come 2028. While the sport is still quite popular and has stabilized in recent years after a steady decline, it is far from its peak in popularity in the mid-2000s and isn't on the rise as it was when "Days of Thunder" was released in 1990. 

A new blockbuster sequel with plenty of firepower in the main cast could be the breath of fresh air NASCAR needs as it tries to regain the appeal it once had to the American masses. 

Samuel Stubbs

Hailing from the same neck of the woods as NASCAR Hall of Famer Mark Martin, Samuel has been covering NASCAR for Yardbarker since February 2024. He has been a member of the National Motorsports Press Association (NMPA) since October of 2024. When he’s not writing about racing, Samuel covers Arkansas Razorback basketball for Yardbarker

NASCAR

NASCAR Cup Series Chase field set after Daytona

Following Saturday's Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona, the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Chase field is set. Here's what the Chase standings look like ahead of the Sept. 6 Chase opener at Darlington Raceway. 1. Denny Hamlin (+25) Hamlin already had the No. 1 seed sewn up going into Daytona and finished 11th on Saturday, coming up one spot short of an 18th top 10 on the season. 2. Ryan Blaney (-25) Blaney finished 33rd on Saturday after crashing on the final lap, but he's sure to be a major player in the championship race. It'd be shocking if he's not in title contention at Homestead on Nov. 8. 3. Tyler Reddick (-35). Reddick stole the No. 3 seed from Ty Gibbs in the closing laps with a clutch third-place finish and nearly winning his sixth race of the season. 4. Ty Gibbs (-40) Gibbs also finished 34th after a last-lap crash, which allowed Reddick to shockingly overtake him for third in the standings. The regular season was a good one for Gibbs, who earned the first two wins of his career at Bristol and Iowa. 5. Chase Briscoe (-45) Briscoe led 10 laps on Saturday and finished 14th to cap what was a solid summer from the No. 19 team going into the Chase. 6. Christopher Bell (-50) Bell wasn't much of a factor on Saturday and finished 16th, but he's caught fire recently and should be a title contender. He's also looking for his first victory of the season over the final 10 races. 7. Kyle Larson (-55) Larson ran up front late but had to pit with his teammates in Chase Elliott and William Byron, which took him out of contention. He also crashed on the final lap and finished 31st. Like Bell, Larson is still searching for his first win of 2026 as he tries to defend his 2025 title. 8. Chase Elliott (-60) Elliott led 19 laps on Saturday and was very fast, but finished 23rd. He needs a good result to kick off the Chase at Darlington after a rough summer stretch. 9. Joey Logano (-65) Surprisingly, Logano only led two laps on Saturday and finished 18th. Regardless of what happened at Daytona, however, he's come on strong as of late. 10. Chris Buescher (-70) Buescher was in position to win Stage 1 on Sunday before he spun and broke a toe link on his No. 17 Ford. He finished last (40th), 15 laps down. 11. Daniel Suarez (-75) Suarez didn't run well all night, but found his way to the front late and finished second after a chaotic final lap. 12. Carson Hocevar (-80) Hocevar was in contention late but crashed on Lap 156, completing a horrendous four-week span for the No. 77 team that leaves it with no momentum going into the Chase. 13. William Byron (-85) Byron, a three-time winner at Daytona, was very fast in Stage 3 but only finished 22nd. He's also winless this season and could use a win early in the Chase. 14. Bubba Wallace (-90) Wallace clinched a Chase berth after Stage 1 on Sunday but only finished 20th after pitting for fuel just before the final restart. 15. Austin Cindric (-95) The Chase cut line got dicey for Cindric in the closing laps, but he brought his No. 2 Team Penske Ford home in sixth and sewed up a Chase berth. 16. Ryan Preece (-100) Preece clearly has a flair for the dramatic at Daytona, as he won his way into the Chase and scored career win No. 1 on Saturday. Regardless of how his final 10 races go, Saturday's race was an unforgettable moment for the No. 60 team.

NFL

The Lions are making their most shocking cut we’ve ever seen, and I don’t understand it

Dortch appeared positioned to fill a role on offense and compete for the punt-return job after a strong summer, making Detroit’s decision one of its biggest cutdown-day surprises. The Detroit Lions are releasing wide receiver Greg Dortch, and I genuinely do not know why they’re doing this. It makes zero sense to me. I thought Dortch had a really good summer. I thought he had earned the punt return job. I thought he had earned the kick returner job. This is one of the most shocking roster cuts I have ever seen the Lions make, and that is not hyperbole. This was on absolutely nobody’s radar. Not a single person thought this would happen. Part of me wonders if this is some sort of mistake. Dortch has history with offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. He was someone I expected to be a big part of Detroit’s offense in terms of gadget plays and versatility. He can do a bunch of different things, and he showed that throughout camp. He’s been good this summer. I just don’t know what happened. What does the Lions’ receiver room look like now? You can look at this and start to piece together what the thought process might be. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Isaac TeSlaa are your top three receivers. That was never in question. We thought Dortch would be the clear No. 4, but now the picture changes. Maybe the Lions feel they can’t let go of Tay Martin because they feel too good about what he brings on special teams. Lucky Jackson is someone I think Detroit really likes. I know Lions coach Dan Campbell talked about Jackson a few weeks ago, and the staff seems genuinely high on what he’s able to bring to the table. Then there’s Tom Kennedy, who was in that fight for the punt return job as well. Maybe Kennedy found his way onto the roster at this point. So I’m thinking out loud here, but the receiver room could shape up as six guys: St. Brown, Williams, TeSlaa, Martin, Jackson, and Kennedy. Was there a sign we missed? It was a bit of a surprise to see Dortch playing in the third preseason game. Maybe that could have been a sign. But a bunch of guys played in that game, so it didn’t stand out as a red flag at the time. I’m almost at a loss for words. I’ve got to say it again. This is the most shocking cut I’ve ever seen this team make. We’re going to see what happens next, whether Dortch clears waivers or another team scoops him up. But for Detroit, this is a stunner.

NFL

Bears' roster cuts include two preseason stars, local veteran

The Chicago Bears announced over 30 players were released or waived on Sunday. NFL teams had until 6 p.m. ET on Sunday to reduce their rosters to 53 players. Among the players released or waived by the Bears were preseason stars such as running back Salvon Ahmed, wide receiver Maurice Alexander and Barrington native and fellow pass-catcher Scotty Miller. Ahmed starred for the Bears in their preseason-opening 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns, notching three receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown and adding two carries for 17 yards. He was among the Bears released as a vested veteran, making him a free agent. Ahmed showed promise in the first two preseason games, but did not play at Tennessee. Alexander led the Bears with 15 receptions, 152 receiving yards and two touchdowns in the preseason. Miller, who has played seven years in the NFL with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Atlanta Falcons and Pittsburgh Steelers, had seven receptions for 65 yards in the preseason. In 93 career NFL games, Miller has 99 receptions for 1,216 yards and six touchdowns. The Bears have a deep WR corps. Rookie Zavion Thomas, who starred for the Bears in Saturday's 24-15 win at Tennessee, made the team. There was some speculation that Thomas might be placed on the practice squad. He had five receptions for 140 yards and a scintillating 97-yard TD reception against Tennessee. Other notable preseason transactions for Chicago Bears Other notable moves by the Bears on Sunday were placing defensive back Kyler Gordon, linebacker Noah Sewell and defensive lineman Shemar Turner on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. Gordon, Sewell and Turner will be out for at least the first four games in the regular season. Running back Brittain Brown, LB Tony Fields, DB Jaylon Jones and WR Ray-Ray McCloud III were placed on injured reserve. The Bears open the regular season on Sept. 13 at noon at the Carolina Panthers on Fox. The home opener is on Sept. 20 at noon against the Minnesota Vikings, also on Fox. On Sept. 28, the Bears will make their 2026 national-television debut against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football."

MLB

Bo Bichette shares new admission about early struggles with Mets

New York Mets infielder Bo Bichette previously acknowledged that he felt his slow start to the season contributed to the Mets falling to last place in the National League East standings amid what has become a woeful season for the 61-76 club. As MLB insider Chelsea Janes of SNY detailed over the weekend, Bichette recently shared a new admission about making the move to the Big Apple after the 28-year-old played for the Toronto Blue Jays from 2019-25. Bo Bichette finally feels he is a good fit with Mets? "I’ve never been someone that is super open right away," Bichette explained. "But it has definitely been different. In Toronto, for the most part, for six years it was kind of my clubhouse along with [Vladimir Guerrero Jr.]. And so coming here and figuring out where I belong and whose word is the last word and all of that kind of stuff – I was trying to figure it out. But as the season’s gone along, I feel like I fit in where I need to fit in." Last offseason, Bichette signed a three-year, $126M deal that included opt-outs after the first and second years to join the Mets. He later ended an 0-for-16 slump on June 3, and he has since been a positive for the Mets as both a player and a behind-the-scenes figure. Per Baseball Reference, Bichette slashed .304/.344/.467 with an .811 OPS, nine home runs and 38 RBI over his last 74 games through Sunday. "I think just one day I kind of let it all go and started playing better," Bichette said about his improved numbers. "I don’t necessarily think I found me for a long time after that. But I was still able to come here and compete and put up numbers, which I was not able to do at the beginning." Mets have big Bo Bichette wish On Aug. 20, MLB insider Jon Heyman of the New York Post reported that "the chances for Bo Bichette to opt out with $84M and another opt-out opportunity are zero." Bichette has not yet confirmed that's the case, but young outfielder Carson Benge is among the Mets players who are hoping that Heyman's update proves to be accurate. "Obviously, we all want him to stay," Benge said about Bichette. "At the end of the day, it’s his choice, his career. Whatever he chooses, I’ll wish him the best. But we obviously want him to stay." The Mets may not learn of Bichette's intentions until after they wrap up their season on Sept. 27.
